verses.1: Yet for this my heart quakes and departs from its place.
verses.2: Listen, listen to the roar of His voice, for from His mouth it comes forth.
verses.3: He spreads it out beneath all the heavens, and His light upon the wings of the earth.
verses.4: Behind it He shouts with a voice, He thunders in the voice of His glory, and He does not spare them, for His voice is heard.
verses.5: He thunders, the mighty in His voice, doing wonders, great works which we do not know.
verses.6: For to the snow He says, “Fall on the earth,” and to the rain, and to the rain of His might.
verses.7: In the hand of every man He seals, that all the sons of men may know His work.
verses.8: And the wild beasts come under the covert, and they rest in their dens.
verses.9: From the chamber comes a storm, and from the cold of the north, cold.
verses.10: By the breath of God He gives frost; the waters are frozen at His word.
verses.11: Also, He appoints a cloud for the rain, scatters His light through the cloud.
verses.12: And He turns the clouds in circles, His paths are in their wheels, doing all He has commanded them upon the face of the earth’s wheel.
verses.13: Whether for a rod, or for the land, or for lovingkindness, He will find it.
verses.14: Attend to this, Job. Stand and consider the wonders of God.
verses.15: Do you know when God sets them in place, and makes His light appear from the cloud?
verses.16: Do you know how He spreads out the layers of the cloud, the wondrous works of the Perfect One?
verses.17: Who among you makes your garment warm, and the quiet land still from the south?
verses.18: He fastens the vault with you, strong as a molten mirror.
verses.19: What can we say to Him? We cannot form words in the face of His darkness.
verses.20: Will it be told to Him that I speak? If a man speaks, will it be consumed?
verses.21: And now, they have not seen bright light, it is hidden in the clouds, and the wind passes and purges them.
verses.22: From the north, golden radiance comes — on God, a terrible splendor.
verses.23: The Almighty — no one can find Him, great in might and in justice, and abundant in righteousness — He does not oppress.
verses.24: Therefore, let men fear Him; none of the wise of heart sees Him.

notes:
Notes
- v. 12: "His paths are in their wheels" — the Hebrew text uses poetic imagery of cyclical movement, which is captured here to reflect the divine orchestration of the clouds.
raw:
[1] Yet for this my heart quakes and departs from its place.

[2] Listen, listen to the roar of His voice, for from His mouth it comes forth.

[3] He spreads it out beneath all the heavens, and His light upon the wings of the earth.

[4] Behind it He shouts with a voice, He thunders in the voice of His glory, and He does not spare them, for His voice is heard.

[5] He thunders, the mighty in His voice, doing wonders, great works which we do not know.

[6] For to the snow He says, “Fall on the earth,” and to the rain, and to the rain of His might.

[7] In the hand of every man He seals, that all the sons of men may know His work.

[8] And the wild beasts come under the covert, and they rest in their dens.

[9] From the chamber comes a storm, and from the cold of the north, cold.

[10] By the breath of God He gives frost; the waters are frozen at His word.

[11] Also, He appoints a cloud for the rain, scatters His light through the cloud.

[12] And He turns the clouds in circles, His paths are in their wheels, doing all He has commanded them upon the face of the earth’s wheel.

[13] Whether for a rod, or for the land, or for lovingkindness, He will find it.

[14] Attend to this, Job. Stand and consider the wonders of God.

[15] Do you know when God sets them in place, and makes His light appear from the cloud?

[16] Do you know how He spreads out the layers of the cloud, the wondrous works of the Perfect One?

[17] Who among you makes your garment warm, and the quiet land still from the south?

[18] He fastens the vault with you, strong as a molten mirror.

[19] What can we say to Him? We cannot form words in the face of His darkness.

[20] Will it be told to Him that I speak? If a man speaks, will it be consumed?

[21] And now, they have not seen bright light, it is hidden in the clouds, and the wind passes and purges them.

[22] From the north, golden radiance comes — on God, a terrible splendor.

[23] The Almighty — no one can find Him, great in might and in justice, and abundant in righteousness — He does not oppress.

[24] Therefore, let men fear Him; none of the wise of heart sees Him.
